cards.explanation: The answer is Moses, Aaron and the whole congregation. The text says the finders brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation (Numbers 15:33). Moses is the one God sent to bring Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10), and Aaron is his brother, whom God set apart to serve as priest (Exodus 28:1). So this went straight to the leaders and the whole congregation, friends, not a quiet word in somebody's ear.

The answer is hold. The text says that because it had not been declared what should be done to him, they placed him in custody (Numbers 15:34). He was held while the question was still open. Think of a batch sitting in the oven with the timer still running, friends. Nobody pulls it out until the time is up, and nobody decided early.

The answer is that he must be put to death, and friends, it's a heavy one. The LORD tells Moses, "The man must surely be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him outside the camp." (Numbers 15:35) That's the answer the people had been waiting for. It's a hard line to read, and I won't pretend otherwise.

The answer is tassels. God tells them to make tassels for the corners of their garments, with a blue cord on each tassel (Numbers 15:38). That's a small thing to wear, but it sits right there on every corner, bakers. I'd still lose mine in the dough by lunchtime.

The answer is all of God's commandments. God says the tassels are "…for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD…" (Numbers 15:39). One glance down and there's the reminder. It works like a sticky note on the oven door, friends, except mine always ends up covered in flour.

The answer is False. God says the tassels are so they may remember the commandments of the LORD and obey them, "…and not prostitute yourselves by following your own heart and your own eyes." (Numbers 15:39) The tassels point away from following their own heart and eyes, not toward it. It's a tricky one, friends, because the verse names the heart and eyes right at the end, and that's easy to grab onto.

The answer is True. God says, "Then you will remember and obey all My commandments, and you will be holy to your God." (Numbers 15:40) Remembering and obeying go together in that line, friends, and the result is being holy to Him. That's a quote worth keeping on the counter.

The answer is Egypt. God says He is the LORD their God "…who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Numbers 15:41) He's reminding them who He is and what He did for them. That's a good thing to hear before you head back to the oven, bakers.
